summary: Most of the new money in healthcare is still going to obesity drugs: Lilly guides to $85 to $87 billion of 2026 revenue as GLP-1 volume rises 60% while prices fall. Big pharma is also buying one-time genetic medicines (Lilly bought Verve, AbbVie bought Capstan) just as the first in vivo CRISPR drug heads for FDA filing, and surgical robots now have three US rivals to Intuitive. AI diagnostics and brain implants draw heavy venture money, but reimbursement codes, not technology, are what hold them back.

innovations.name: In vivo gene editing and cell therapy
innovations.what: One-time treatments that edit genes inside the body, or turn a patient's own T cells into CAR-T cells inside the body, with no lab manufacturing step. The goal is to replace a lifetime of pills or infusions with one dose.
innovations.stage_why: The first in vivo CRISPR drug (Intellia's lonvo-z for hereditary angioedema) has phase 3 data and a rolling FDA filing, with launch hoped for in H1 2027. The ex vivo version (Casgevy) is on the market but still small at $76 million in Q2 2026.

evidence.cost: Ex vivo therapies need weeks of cell manufacturing and a hospital stay. In vivo versions are one infusion, which should lower cost per patient over time, but no launch price for an in vivo edit exists yet.
evidence.approvals: Casgevy approved in the US and expanded to children 2 and older (2026). Intellia started a rolling BLA for lonvo-z in HAE, completion expected H2 2026. Nex-z phase 3 trials in ATTR paused in late 2025 and have resumed screening.
evidence.money: Lilly bought Verve for about $1.3 billion (2025) for one-shot LDL lowering. AbbVie paid $2.1 billion for Capstan (in vivo CAR-T, June 2025); BMS paid $1.5 billion for Orbital; AstraZeneca paid $425 million upfront for EsoBiotec; Gilead paid $350 million upfront for Interius.
evidence.revenue: Vertex Casgevy revenue $76 million in Q2 2026, up 151% year over year and up 78% from Q1. Sarepta Elevidys (AAV gene therapy) fell to $98.1 million in Q2 2026 from $281.9 million after a narrower label.

spreads_to.use: One-time editing of PCSK9 or ANGPTL3 to lower LDL and triglycerides for life (Verve/Lilly, CRISPR Therapeutics CTX310).
In vivo CAR-T to reset the immune system in lupus and other B cell diseases without chemotherapy.
The same CRISPR tools and licenses edit crops and livestock (for example the PRRS-resistant pig).

innovations.bottleneck: Delivery. Lipid nanoparticles that reach the liver or T cells safely are held by a few developers and licensors, and one liver safety event can pause a whole program, as nex-z showed.

next_milestone.event: Intellia completes the lonvo-z BLA; FDA decision and first in vivo CRISPR launch
next_milestone.timing: BLA completion H2 2026; launch targeted H1 2027

innovations.thesis_broken_if: FDA rejects lonvo-z or a new death or liver injury halts in vivo editing trials across companies.

innovations.name: AI diagnostics and imaging
innovations.what: Software that reads scans, slides, ECGs and genomic data to flag disease faster than a doctor working alone. Most of it rides on the scanners and lab tests hospitals already use.
innovations.stage_why: Over 1,500 AI devices are FDA cleared and Tempus runs at a $1.6 billion revenue pace, but Medicare pays for very few AI reads directly, so most hospitals buy AI only when it saves staff time.

evidence.approvals: FDA AI-enabled device list reached 1,524, mostly radiology. Aidoc won the first FDA clearance for a foundation model based imaging triage system in 2026. As of January 2026 there are only two CPT Category I payment codes for newer AI.
evidence.money: Aidoc raised a $150 million Series E (April 2026) led by Goldman Sachs Alternatives with NVentures (Nvidia) and SoftBank; total funding over $500 million. Tempus signed about $200 million of new data and application licenses in Q2 2026.
evidence.revenue: Tempus Q2 2026 revenue $382.5 million, up 22%; 2026 guide raised to $1.595 to $1.605 billion with about $65 million adjusted EBITDA; data licensing revenue up 36%.

spreads_to.use: De-identified clinical and genomic data licensed to drug makers to pick trial patients and targets.
Earlier detection used in value-based care contracts to cut late-stage treatment costs.
AI reading of wearable ECG and sensor data at home (Apple Watch, Oura, Zio patches).

innovations.bottleneck: Reimbursement codes and labeled clinical data. CMS and the AMA CPT panel control payment, and the scanner installed base (GE HealthCare, Siemens Healthineers, Philips) controls where AI gets deployed.

next_milestone.event: CY2027 Medicare Physician Fee Schedule final rule, which sets any new AI payment
next_milestone.timing: Usually early November; expected around November 2026

innovations.thesis_broken_if: Medicare keeps AI bundled into existing payments through 2027 and Tempus growth falls below 15%.

innovations.name: GLP-1 and next gen metabolic drugs
innovations.what: Weekly shots and now daily pills that cut appetite and treat diabetes, heart, liver and sleep apnea risk. The next wave adds amylin and triple agonists for 25% to 30% weight loss.
innovations.stage_why: Lilly's Q2 2026 volume rose 60% and two oral pills launched in 2026. Medicare now covers them with a $50 copay via the GLP-1 Bridge from July 2026, so this is a mass market where price per patient is falling.

evidence.cost: Lilly realized prices fell 13% in Q2 2026. Foundayo launched at $149 a month self pay for the starting dose. Medicare negotiated semaglutide price is $274 a month from January 2027 versus $959 list.
evidence.approvals: Wegovy pill launched in the US January 5, 2026; FDA approved Lilly's orforglipron (Foundayo) April 1, 2026. CagriSema filed December 2025.
evidence.money: Lilly is building US API sites in Virginia ($5 billion), Houston ($6.5 billion) and Huntsville ($6 billion). Pfizer paid about $10 billion for Metsera (closed November 2025).
evidence.revenue: Lilly Q2 2026 revenue $23.0 billion, up 48%; Mounjaro $9.9 billion (+91%) and Zepbound $4.9 billion (+46%). Weekly prescriptions about 181,000 for Wegovy pill and about 44,000 for Foundayo (September 2026 tracker).

spreads_to.use: Smaller portions and higher protein demand; snack volumes under pressure.
Fewer obesity-related procedures over time, but more CGM and heart monitoring for treated patients.
Biggest new pharmacy cost line; drives PBM and benefit design changes.

innovations.bottleneck: Drug substance capacity: peptide API for injectables and large-scale small molecule API for pills. Lilly and Novo control most of it and Lilly is bringing more in house.
innovations.thesis_broken_if: Volume growth slows to match price cuts so Lilly's revenue growth falls under 15%, or a new class-wide safety warning cuts new starts.

innovations.name: Neurotech and brain computer interfaces
innovations.what: Implants that read brain signals so paralyzed people can type, speak or move a cursor, plus newer stimulators that adjust themselves to brain activity. Long term goal is restoring speech, vision and movement.
innovations.stage_why: Dozens of people have implants in feasibility trials, but no motor or speech BCI has full FDA approval and Medicare has no payment pathway yet. Synchron plans the first pivotal trial in 2026.

evidence.approvals: Precision Neuroscience got 510(k) clearance for its Layer 7 cortical array for up to 30 days of implantation. Paradromics received an IDE for its Connect-One speech trial. Neuralink has breakthrough device status for speech and vision. No PMA for a long-term BCI yet.
evidence.money: Neuralink raised a $650 million Series E in April 2026 at about $9 billion (about $1.85 billion raised in total). Synchron raised a $200 million Series D (November 2025) to fund its pivotal trial.
evidence.revenue: Almost none for implant BCIs. ClearPoint Neuro, which supplies neurosurgical navigation to more than 60 partner programs, cut its 2026 revenue guide to $48 to $52 million from $52 to $56 million.

spreads_to.use: Brain and nerve signal inputs for glasses and computers (for example Meta's wrist EMG band).
Brain delivery and monitoring tools used in gene therapy trials for Parkinson's and other diseases.
Research on hands-free control of systems (early, mostly government funded).

innovations.bottleneck: High channel count electrodes in hermetic, long-lasting packages, plus neurosurgeon time. The bigger gate is CMS coverage: FDA approval alone does not create payment.

next_milestone.event: Synchron starts its US pivotal trial; Neuralink expands implant numbers

innovations.thesis_broken_if: No BCI company starts a pivotal trial by end of 2027, or a serious implant failure leads FDA to slow the field.

innovations.name: Surgical and procedural robotics
innovations.what: Robot arms that surgeons control from a console, plus robots for knees, spines and prostates. They are sold once and then earn money on every procedure through instruments and service.
innovations.stage_why: Intuitive did about 889,000 procedures in Q2 2026 (up 15%), so the core is proven, but most surgeries worldwide are still not robotic and real US competition only began with Medtronic Hugo (December 2025) and J&J Ottava (July 2026).

evidence.approvals: Medtronic Hugo FDA cleared for urology in December 2025. J&J Ottava received FDA De Novo authorization July 22, 2026 for ten general surgery procedures.
evidence.money: Hospitals keep buying: Intuitive placed 468 systems in Q2 2026, including 246 da Vinci 5.
evidence.revenue: Intuitive Q2 2026 revenue $2.89 billion, up 19%, with most of it recurring instruments, accessories and service.

spreads_to.use: Shorter stays and more outpatient surgery; robots help recruit surgeons.
Shared parts: precision motors, reducers, force sensors and vision.
Video and motion data from millions of cases used to train surgical AI and autonomy features.

innovations.bottleneck: The installed base and surgeon training. Intuitive controls most consoles and training pipelines, so switching costs are high; rivals need years of clinical data per procedure.

next_milestone.event: Intuitive Q3 2026 results: procedure growth and da Vinci 5 placements

innovations.thesis_broken_if: Intuitive procedure growth drops below 10% or new rivals start a price war on systems and instruments.
